# 1 Chronicles Chapter 29 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 385r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/1CH_029_page_001.jpg

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** King David said to the whole assembly: "Solomon my son, whom alone God has chosen, is young and inexperienced, and the work is great, for the temple is not for man but for the LORD God.

**2** "So I have provided for the house of my God, with all my resources — gold for the things of gold, silver for the things of silver, bronze for the things of bronze, iron for the things of iron, and wood for the things of wood; onyx stones, stones for setting, antimony, colored stones, every kind of precious stone, and marble — all in great quantity.

**3** "Moreover, because of my devotion to the house of my God, I give my personal treasure of gold and silver to the house of my God, over and above all that I have provided for the holy house: **4** three thousand talents of gold, of the gold of Ophir, and seven thousand talents of refined silver, for overlaying the walls of the house; **5** gold for the things of gold and silver for the things of silver, and for all the work to be done by craftsmen. Who then is willing to consecrate himself today to the LORD?"

**6** Then the leaders of the ancestral houses, the officers of the tribes of Israel, the commanders of thousands and hundreds, and the officers over the king's work gave willingly. **7** They gave for the service of the house of God: five thousand talents and ten thousand darics of gold, ten thousand talents of silver, eighteen thousand talents of bronze, and one hundred thousand talents of iron. **8** Whoever had precious stones gave them to the treasury of the house of the LORD, in the care of Jehiel the Gershonite.

**9** The people rejoiced over the freewill offerings, for they gave to the LORD with a whole heart. King David also rejoiced greatly.

**10** Then David blessed the LORD in the presence of all the assembly. David said: "Blessed are you, O LORD, the God of Israel our father, forever and ever.

**11** "Yours, O LORD, is the greatness and the power and the glory and the victory and the majesty, for all that is in the heavens and in the earth is yours. Yours is the kingdom, O LORD, and you are exalted as head above all.

**12** "Both riches and honor come from you, and you rule over all. In your hand are power and might, and in your hand it is to make great and to give strength to all.

**13** "And now we thank you, our God, and praise your glorious name.

**14** "But who am I, and what is my people, that we should be able to give as generously as this? For all things come from you, and of your own have we given you.

**15** "For we are strangers before you and sojourners, as all our fathers were. Our days on earth are like a shadow, and there is no abiding.

**16** "O LORD our God, all this abundance that we have provided for building you a house for your holy name comes from your hand, and all of it is yours.

**17** "I know, my God, that you test the heart and delight in uprightness. In the uprightness of my heart I have freely given all these things, and now I have seen with joy your people who are present here giving freely to you.

**18** "O LORD, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, our fathers, keep this forever as the intention of the thoughts of the hearts of your people, and direct their hearts toward you. **19** Grant to Solomon my son a whole heart to keep your commandments, your testimonies, and your statutes, and to do them all, and to build the temple for which I have made provision."

**20** Then David said to the whole assembly, "Bless the LORD your God." And all the assembly blessed the LORD, the God of their fathers, and bowed their heads and paid homage to the LORD and to the king.

**21** They offered sacrifices to the LORD and offered burnt offerings to the LORD on the next day — a thousand bulls, a thousand rams, a thousand lambs, with their drink offerings, and sacrifices in abundance for all Israel.

**22** They ate and drank before the LORD on that day with great gladness. They made Solomon the son of David king a second time, and they anointed him as ruler for the LORD, and Zadok as priest.

**23** Then Solomon sat on the throne of the LORD as king in place of David his father. He prospered, and all Israel obeyed him. **24** All the leaders and the mighty men, and also all the sons of King David, pledged their allegiance to King Solomon.

**25** The LORD made Solomon exceedingly great in the sight of all Israel and bestowed on him royal majesty such as had not been on any king before him in Israel.

**26** Thus David the son of Jesse reigned over all Israel. **27** The time that he reigned over Israel was forty years: he reigned seven years in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem.

**28** He died at a good old age, full of days, riches, and honor. Solomon his son reigned in his place.

**29** Now the acts of King David, from first to last, are written in the chronicles of Samuel the seer, and in the chronicles of Nathan the prophet, and in the chronicles of Gad the seer, **30** with accounts of all his reign and his might, and of the events that befell him and Israel and all the kingdoms of the lands.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

The theological climax of 1 Chronicles. David's prayer (vv.10-19) is the Chronicler's magnum opus — a meditation on divine sovereignty, human transience, and the paradox of generosity. The five-fold doxology (v.11) became one of the most consequential liturgical texts in history, echoed in the Lord's Prayer's doxology and in Jewish daily worship. The central insight — "of your own have we given you" (v.14) — dissolves the boundary between giving and receiving. David dies in the Chronicler's ideal: peaceful, satisfied, honored, with an orderly succession. The absence of Bathsheba, Absalom, Amnon, and every shadow of 2 Samuel is not naivety but theology — the Chronicler presents the David who matters for worship, the David whose prayer can still be prayed. The closing formula (vv.29-30) cites three prophetic sources — Samuel, Nathan, Gad — establishing that David's story was documented by multiple witnesses, the Chronicler's version being the definitive synthesis. The phrase "the throne of the LORD" (v.23) is the Chronicler's distinctive theology of kingship: the human king occupies God's own throne as regent, not as sovereign.

---
## Disagreement Log

### V.1 — "temple" vs. "fortress/palace" (*birah*)
- **EMET:** "the-fortress [ha-birah]"
- **LOGOS:** "the temple"
- **PNEUMA:** "this palace"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "the temple" — while *birah* literally means fortress/palace (a Persian loanword), in context it refers to the temple complex. LOGOS's rendering is clearest for the English reader, though the Persian loanword is noted.

### V.5 — "to consecrate himself" vs. "to fill his hand"
- **EMET:** "to-fill [le-malle] his-hand [yado]" (priestly consecration idiom)
- **LOGOS:** "to consecrate himself"
- **PNEUMA:** "to consecrate themselves"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "to consecrate himself" — the idiom *mille yad* means to consecrate/ordain. EMET's literal rendering preserves the priestly overtone but would confuse English readers.

### V.14 — "retain strength to give" vs. "be able to give"
- **EMET:** "that-we-should-retain-strength [ki na'atsor koach] to-volunteer"
- **LOGOS:** "that we should be able to give as generously as this"
- **PNEUMA:** "that we could give anything at all"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS rendering. The Hebrew *na'atsor koach* (retain/muster strength) is an idiom for having the capacity/ability. PNEUMA's "anything at all" intensifies beyond the Hebrew.

### V.15 — "no abiding" vs. "nothing certain" vs. "no hope"
- **EMET:** "there-is-no hope [eyn miqveh]"
- **LOGOS:** "there is no abiding"
- **PNEUMA:** "nothing certain"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "there is no abiding" — *miqveh* here means "expectation of permanence," not "hope" in the emotional sense. LOGOS captures this. PNEUMA's "nothing certain" is close but less precise.

### V.24 — "gave a hand under" vs. "pledged allegiance"
- **EMET:** "gave [natnu] a-hand [yad] under [tachat]"
- **LOGOS:** "pledged their allegiance to"
- **PNEUMA:** "pledged themselves to"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "pledged their allegiance to" — the Hebrew idiom *natan yad tachat* means to submit/pledge loyalty. LOGOS renders the idiom naturally.

---
*— SOPHIA, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
